normative_summary: Asset Management alone generates canonical lowercase UUID-v4 assetId; clients only reference it.
imageRef and fontRef are atomic ValueTypes with exact closed {assetId} wire.
Missing, non-v4, noncanonical, null, or unknown AssetRef structure is a non-confirmable hard error.
Expected Asset kind derives only from declared ValueType.
DesignDSL forbids content version, hash, URL, file, Profile, or dynamic selector in AssetRef.
Save or recheck recursively extracts every authored AssetRef atom from the authoritative AST.
Extraction includes baselines, defaults, literals, mapping cases, and list atoms regardless of override, use, or reachability.
Every atom creates a distinct dependency occurrence with asset, kind, pointer, and available stable entity locators.
Repeated assetId occurrences cannot be collapsed away.
Active-current dependency projection atomically replaces current occurrences; history is excluded.
Authoritative recheck always re-extracts the AST; projection is never a second fact source.
Delete proof may batch queries but retains every occurrence and hashes a stable sorted tuple set.
Runtime pruning or resolved current never rewrites authored projection or report facts.
After closure freeze, Render re-admits every authored Asset occurrence of each unique snapshot.
A shared snapshot is admitted once, not per invocation.
Closure Asset admission checks same scope, existence, ACTIVE, and immutable kind.
Closure admission reads no user metadata, pins no contentVersion, and creates no snapshot, lock, or long lease.
Physical reads may merge by scope, asset, and kind while diagnostics retain every occurrence.
Problems use stable bounded root, edge, and pointer order and do not leak unreadable child Asset identities.
Admission releases its read boundary; later resolves independently observe later current state.
Readiness or STALE projection is not request authorization truth.
Every root PUBLIC override Asset atom is admitted even if unused.
Override admission requires same scope, existence, ACTIVE, kind, and caller asset.read.
Cross-scope, missing, or unreadable override returns NOT_FOUND.
A valid override produces a request-only nonpersistent AdmittedAssetValue.
AdmittedAssetValue may traverse definitions, mappings, bindings, and fills without repeated actor authorization.
Every final property consumer independently resolves Asset current.
Authored Asset values use internal same-scope Resolver after root Render authorization, without per-Asset caller read.
Root render and external override authorization are checked once at request admission.
Later permission drift does not cancel the admitted request or reauthorize Resolver or lease.
A new request reauthorizes; actor-specific failure never changes TemplateReadiness.
Only a concrete validated AssetRef consumed by a materialized Node property creates a resolve occurrence.
Unused definitions, defaults, or branches do not resolve.
One memoized Asset value consumed by multiple properties creates one occurrence per property.
Every Text Run fontRef is independently resolved.
Resolve occurrence locator is closed OccurrencePath plus ConsumerPropertyRef.
ConsumerPropertyRef reuses closed TargetPropertyRef shape and selector-depth constraints without requiring BindingPolicy.
Resolve order is materialized authored DFS, property declaration order, then Run index.
Resolution occurs immediately after concrete value and aggregate validation.
Speculative or unordered resolution is forbidden; first demanded failure stops later Resolver, capability, and Asset work.
RenderResource manifest preserves resolve encounter order.
render:false, false Conditional, zero Repeat, and SKIP structures prune before resolve.
visible:false and opacity:0 still resolve, fetch, decode, and measure and retain failures.
AssetResolver is a narrow internal Asset Management interface, not a capability or downloader.
Resolver input is limited to request, scope, resource, asset, kind, audience, and deadline.
Occurrence, Template, actor, runtime data, and expression results cannot cross into Asset Management.
Resolve linearization atomically validates scope, lifecycle, and kind, selects current immutable content, and commits idempotency record.
Record key is requestId and resourceId and binds fingerprint, exact selection, lease, issuedAt, and expiresAt.
Selection succeeds only after record commit.
Same key and fingerprint retry reconstructs identical contentVersion and lease.
The same key with different input conflicts.
Only bounded same-key, fingerprint, and deadline retries are allowed for precommit transient failures.
Unknown commit must query the record before retry.
Precommit retry may see new current; postcommit retry never reselects current.
Resolver records are encrypted and expire after lease plus retry margin.
A Resolver record is not audit, history, transcript, query, log, or backup data.
Cancel does not revoke a lease; record and lease expire together.
Successful resolve issues a short-lived Renderer-only HTTPS lease.
Lease claims bind audience, request, resource, asset, content identities, hash, length, and expiry.
Expiry uses UTC RFC3339 and covers render deadline plus exact safety margin; otherwise resolve fails.
A lease reads exact immutable bytes without rechecking current, lifecycle, or actor authorization.
Replace or delete does not revoke a lease; verified pre-expiry bytes remain usable.
Expiry or deadline causes whole Render failure with no renewal or logical re-resolution.
Fetch URL is a request-local bearer secret.
Fetch URL never reaches caller, browser, diagnostic, log, trace, cache, or evaluation identity.
The only domain chain is AssetRef to ResolvedAsset to RenderResource.
ResolvedAsset closed fields are exactly the frozen identity, content, descriptor, lease, and locator set.
OccurrencePath and ConsumerPropertyRef are attached by Rendering after Resolver response.
Every resolve occurrence maps one-to-one to ResolvedAsset and RenderResource without content deduplication.
resourceId is rwres_ plus 64 lowercase SHA-256 hex over the versioned canonical path, property, and kind locator.
A duplicate or colliding resourceId in one manifest is a hard error.
resourceId uniqueness scope is one RenderDocument.
resourceId is not secret, authorization, Asset or global identity, cache key, or cross-request idempotency key.
RenderResource is a closed one-to-one projection with exact frozen Engine fields.
RenderResource excludes asset, content, scope, Template, and business identities.
Node references and manifest entries form an exact one-to-one set and preserve encounter order.
Unknown, null, unused, missing, or duplicate resources fail closed.
sha256 is exactly 64 lowercase hex and acceptanceProfileId is exact v1.
Media type is restricted to frozen image and font values and must match kind.
IMAGE descriptor is closed with exact dimensions, orientation, frame, and color fields.
Image dimensions are positive, frameCount is one, colorEncoding is SRGB_8BIT, and logical size reflects one orientation application.
Image descriptor excludes DPI, metadata bag, raw profile, and filename.
FONT descriptor is closed faceIndex, flavor, and unitsPerEm with faceIndex zero and allowed glyf or CFF flavor.
Font descriptor excludes display, family, license, and system identity.
Stored descriptor is immutable proof while exact bytes remain rendering authority.
Engine fetches, hashes, fully parses, and compares exact image and font bytes before measure or shaping.
Descriptor and byte mismatch is an internal integrity or Profile failure with zero output and no silent choice.
Image pipeline applies orientation and deterministic sRGB to straight RGBA8 before Profile premultiplication.
Font pipeline permits only frozen monochrome single-face outlines and approved layout tables.
Image layout uses oriented logical aspect only and ignores Asset DPI.
Font layout and shaping use only exact bytes and exact Profiles; no system, family, or built-in fallback.
Missing glyph is request runtime failure and does not mutate Asset or Template validity.
User metadata is available only through asset.read product interfaces.
Resolver, ResolvedAsset, RenderResource, digests, and Engine cannot read or carry user metadata.
Metadata changes do not affect selection, digest, readiness, or cache key.
Engine fetch allows canonical HTTPS exact-origin and path-prefix allowlist with segment-boundary matching.
Fetch rejects userinfo, fragment, noncanonical host or port, dot or percent bypass; an empty production allowlist fails closed.
Every connect rechecks DNS and egress policy.
Redirect, proxy, cookie, caller header, range, compression, and fallback are forbidden.
Fetch accepts only a 200 identity body with one matching Content-Length.
The stream verifies budget, actual length, hash, kind, media, magic, and complete decode or parse.
Only transport or 5xx retries are allowed on the same URL, expiry, and deadline.
4xx, expiry, integrity, decode, or Profile failures do not retry.
Engine cannot renew a lease, reread Asset current, or fall back to another URL, font, or content.
Logical current and Resolver result are never shared caches.
Trusted scope cache key is scope, kind, hash, length, and media; decoded cache also keys exact Renderer Profile.
Cross-scope cache sharing is forbidden; Engine without trusted partition is request-local only.
A cache hit never reduces occurrence, budget, or first-error accounting and must validate each lease.
resourceId, unsigned URL, and assetId are not content cache keys.
Cache corruption evicts and fails without fallback or re-resolution.
Resolver selection, descriptor, or lease failure prevents a complete RenderDocument.
Post-seal Engine resource or shaping failure may retain only an internal transient document and returns zero public document or output.
Template dependency uses the frozen TEMPLATE_ASSET codes.
Resolver uses the frozen ASSET_RESOLVE codes.
Engine uses the frozen lease, fetch, integrity, decode, and font codes.
Malformed wire, manifest mismatch, and duplicate or collision are non-confirmable hard errors.
Authored cross-scope ref publicly folds to TEMPLATE_ASSET_NOT_FOUND and may only save INVALID through dependency confirmation.
Runtime failure does not change TemplateReadiness.
Integrity or Profile failure emits a redacted ops signal and never mutates Asset lifecycle or content.
Engine errors expose only stable code, resourceId, and safe parameters.
Rendering maps resourceId to authorized occurrence or property diagnostics; Engine never receives author identities.
Authored assetId is shown only under Template read; a submitted override may echo to its submitter.
Runtime assetId is appended only when the caller also has asset.read.
Problems, logs, and traces prohibit URL, token, hash, version, blob, name, bytes, metadata, and raw-network details.
STALE and Asset lifecycle or content events do not cancel an active Evaluation.
Resolved occurrences stay exact; unresolved occurrences observe later state.
Changes after final resolve do not affect current output; the next Render re-admits.
Authoritative preview always uses the complete Evaluator and Engine.
Draft Asset preview is a separate asset.read interface and the browser never receives a Renderer lease.
A missing, deleted, or kind placeholder is diagnostic-only and is never persisted or auto-substituted.
A lease-bearing RenderDocument is request-only, Renderer-only, nonpersistent, nonpublic, and nonreusable.
Cancel, deadline, or expiry yields zero output with no renewal or document return.
assetSelectionDigest canonically covers each successful selection in encounter order with frozen fields.
URL, token, expiry, cache, and network timing are excluded from selection digest.
A different contentVersion remains different selection identity even for identical bytes.
The ResolvedAsset transcript is request-only.
Persisted Evaluation metadata may retain only digest, count, code, and timing; Asset audit does not log each resolve.
Capacity independently limits all frozen authored, resolved, content, bytes, pixels, fonts, manifest, URL, and fetch dimensions.
Cache cannot reduce occurrence accounting.
Predictable excess fails before the document; Engine independently enforces actual byte and decode hard limits.
A READY Renderer proves the exact acceptance-profile compatible superset with machine manifest and golden corpus.
Renderer Profile owns color, orientation, decoder, OpenType, and raster; Layout Profile owns shaping and layout.
Upgrades cannot silently alter old Profile semantics.
Implementation must support the exact new Render Command, Document, and Layout contracts and missing fields and viewport primitive.
Implementation cannot reuse an old version while dropping fields, guessing versions, or adding placeholders.
Ticket19 conformance covers all listed concurrent selection, retry, lifecycle, pruning, authorization, cache, manifest, integrity, font, path, redaction, and capacity cases.

v1 excludes dynamic content selectors, URL or data refs, public or cross-scope refs, arbitrary HTTP, current cache, redirect, fallback, font fallback, auto replacement, transform, recovery, renewal, skipping, and partial output.
SVG, animation, DOCUMENT, and other media remain out of scope.
Ticket13 creates no product code, API, table, route, placeholder, or implementation phase.
